There's more to running a show than a countdown.

The queue is the product. Timers, displays and rehearsal are properties of it, not bolted-on extras.

Drag-reorder, bulk edit, and a schedule that recalculates when one item runs long.

Dynamic per-event fields

Mic requirements, slides, lighting, camera angle - the Add Item form adapts to the production.

Sections within a session

Multi-day, multi-session events with partitions, not one flat list pretending to scale.

No-login venue displays

A share link, QR code, or 6-digit TV code - nobody in the room needs an account.

Rehearsal without the risk

Run the full sequence end to end without ever touching a connected display.

Built for 200+ item events

Not a countdown tool retrofitted with a queue - the queue was the starting point.

Everything an operator reaches for mid-show.

Bulk edit

Multi-select and change timing, owner or status across items at once.

Live alerts

Multi-day events

Friday Evening, Saturday Morning - each its own session, one event.

Status at a glance

Current, next, on deck, done - every item's state, without asking.

TWO AUDIENCES

Two very different distances from the screen.

The operator drives the whole show.

Laptop at the console or phone backstage. Task-focused, trained on the tool, back in it across every day of a multi-day event.

Everyone else never touches the interface.

Performers, AV crew, presenters, attendees - glancing at a TV or confidence monitor. Reached by link, QR, or a 6-digit TV code. No account, ever.
